_limits_comment: Every measurement below declares limits (issue #154). Without them a
`klt pex` delta[] row's `status: pass` means only that both legs produced
a number -- not that the extracted value is anywhere near the schematic
one; `klt pex` grades a row against the *extracted*-side value's own
declared limits (see klayout-tools' pex.py `_row_status`).
Both bounds are quoted verbatim from spec/target-spec.md's RATIFIED
table, never invented here:
vout_*_v            -- the ratified `Output` row, 1.8V +/-2%, i.e.
vin_minus_vout_*_v  -- the ratified `Dropout @ 50 mA` row, < 300mV, so
max 0.300; min 0 because a regulating pass
device cannot present a negative source-drain
drop, and a negative reading is a non-physical
operating point rather than an unusually good one.
Consequence, stated plainly: these are *spec* bounds, and
measurements/characterization.md already records the schematic-side
implementation as FAIL against both rows at many PVT corners. A failing
row here is therefore not automatically an extraction artifact -- read it
against the same corner's schematic_value in delta[] before attributing
it to the layout.
